page.title: Contacts
page.purpose: Everyone who has ever reached an agent here, and the tier each one holds. This is the security surface of the product: a tier change is the only edit on it, and it is the edit with the largest blast radius.

priorities.statement: Which tier each contact holds, as a rank rather than a category
What a tier actually permits, stated before it is changed
Which rooms a contact is in, because a group's ceiling derives from its roster
That an unrecognised sender is already a stranger and needs no action
What a tier change will do, before it is confirmed

states.description: Contacts are listed with their tier and the rooms they appear in.
Nobody outside the owner has reached an agent yet.

claims.statement: Tier is presented as an ordered ladder from stranger to owner, not as four unordered categories.
claims.rationale: The whole model depends on tiers being comparable, because the room ceiling is a minimum across them.

claims.statement: What a tier permits is stated in plain language before the change is confirmed.
claims.rationale: Nobody can consent to a permission change described only by its name.

claims.statement: Raising or lowering a tier states which group ceilings the change moves, before it is confirmed.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-001 makes a tier change ripple into every room the contact is in. That ripple must not be a surprise.

claims.statement: Promoting a contact to owner is visibly distinct from every other tier change and requires deliberate confirmation.
claims.rationale: Owner is the only tier that can reach an owner-only capability.

claims.statement: The empty state states that unrecognised senders are already strangers and that no action is required.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-009 makes stranger the default. An empty list that implies work is misleading.

claims.statement: A failed tier write restores the previous tier visibly rather than leaving the control in the attempted position.
Tiers are distinguishable without relying on colour alone.
Tier treatments hold their ordering and contrast in both themes.
